root.name: Sicilian Defense: Boleslavsky Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nc6 6. Be2 e5

overview: In the Classical Sicilian Black plays ...e5 at once, kicking the d4 knight and gaining space at the cost of a weak d5 square and a backward d6 pawn. White usually plays Nb3 and Be3, aiming for a knight on d5, while Black develops with ...Be7 and ...O-O. The game is strategic rather than a tactical melee.

white_ideas.idea: Retreat with Nb3 and Be3, then play Nd5 to exploit the hole
Play Bg5 or Ndb5 to disturb Black's set-up

black_ideas.idea: Trade the knight on d5 and use ...d5 or ...b5 at the right moment

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on d6 and e5 against White's e4, with a hole on d5

character.notes: A steady Sicilian where Black gives up the usual counterplay for a solid set-up.

soundness.notes: Sound and respectable; Black is slightly worse but safe.

structure.notes: Semi-open: Sicilian asymmetry with a half-open c-file.

level.notes: Plans around d5 and the backward pawn matter more than theory.

sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nc6 6. Be2 e5 7. Nxc6 bxc6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes with the b-pawn and fights for the centre.

character.reason: Black gives up counterplay for a hard-to-break structure.

structure.reason: Sicilian asymmetry with a half-open file.

plans.reason: White aims at a d5 outpost.
